194.t: Dancing with Streamline Isaac Harris and Harrison Hike
194.s: He learned dances and acrobatic tricks from Streamline Isaac Harris and taught them to a friend; the three did step routines.
194.q: Well, we streamlined Isaac. Streamline who? Streamline Isaac. At that time, he used to go off a lot. And he'd learn all of these different dances and things. And when he'd come back, he would teach them to me.

194.t: Dancing at clubs, the Lincoln Theater and Bourbon Street
194.s: They danced at the Cotton Club and Lincoln Theater and for money on Bourbon Street before he switched to playing music.
194.q: Yeah, at the Lincoln, during the time I played at the Palace of Lincoln I was playing music then. I switched from dancing. But we used to dance all up and down Bourbon.

252.t: Dancers Brown and McGraw and Paul Ash
252.s: She tells of Naomi McGraw and Herbert Brown, New Orleans dancers who learned in the street.
252.q: Paul Ash was a great white band in Chicago. Oh, I have heard of the band. Yeah. Well, now, she was his leading lady in this all-white band. But she never had a lesson of nothing. Her and this Brown just got to dancing among themselves and got up the team. And they was one of the country's top…

176.t: Smiley starting out as an entertainer at the Kingfish
176.s: They started a dancer who played ukulele at the Kingfish by pushing him onto the floor.
176.q: He was playing a ukulele with me at the Kingfish. Start on the ukulele. We had to push him out on the floor. Make him take that yulele on the floor and dance to go mud. You know, that's what he started off. And he'd tell anybody today. He said, Bill and Dee Dee. Start him in that business. Start…

153.t: Tap dancing learned from his sister Mary
153.s: He explains that drummers of the era tap-danced and emceed in the theaters, and that his sister Mary taught him time-step and shim-sham, which helped his left foot on two bass drums.
153.q: All the drummers during that era – Jo Jones, for example, Buddy Rich – Steve Gadd was a Mouseketeer. They all tap-danced. They told jokes. Because when you played the theaters, you did everything. You were m.c. You had a dance routine. You had a dance routine called a b.s. chorus. It was nothing…

367.t: Learning to dance from the Brown Skinned Models show
367.s: Young says he learned time steps while the family band toured with a show he thinks was the Brown Skinned Models.
367.q: I don‘t know…I don‘t know. I was a kid and I learned how to dance. I used to play on the, oh I know how I learned that, I used to play a family band went on the road with a show called the…

406.t: Illinois Jaquet as a tap dancer in Fort Worth
406.s: Barefield first met Jaquet in Fort Worth while with Cab, when he was in an amateur-night tap dance trio with a boxing routine.
406.q: So later on Joe Newman did give me back, but Illinois -- so every time I see Joe now, I say, where's Illinois? I don't know where he is, because he -- you know, he's wild (inaudible) when he gets -- but I knew him, when I first met him, he was a tap dancer.

1.t: Lu's dance partner and the Georgia Grind
1.s: Lu says that at eleven she danced with partner Doug DeLille doing the Georgia Grind, shimmy and tap routines, while Gladys sang blues.
1.ch: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
1.q: Yes. You see, when I was eleven years old, my mother told me that I couldn't sing no more, and that if anybody asked me to be in a concert, to tell them I could dance. So I had a partner called Doug DeLille(?) and I was Louise DuPont. We were partners together, and we did our dance, you know. And I…

378.t: Flaming Youth Revue cast and learning to tap dance
378.s: He describes the troupers, including Virginia Moore and Frank Kulman, and how he picked up tap steps from other acts and later partner Eddie White.
378.q: She did her own single number, I did xylophone numbers -- one of the boys was a piano player, and he was a singer, great voice, he could dance, he was a multiple talented kid. And, the other boy was very young and his mother travelled with us.

385.t: Tap dancing and the Hoofers Club
385.s: He played piano for dancers at the Hoofers Club and learned to dance himself, which led to an off-Broadway show.
385.q: Q. Dancing I was a tap dancer. I was very much in earnest. I tried everything to be in show business. They had a place called the Hoofers Club, the Rhythm club. And all the fellas used to meet down there, when they had nowhere else to go. Nothin' but dancers.

170.t: Tap dancing and the tramp-band mugger
170.s: He learns tap dancing from his father and describes how dancers and a mugger fronted the tramp bands.
